evidence: Template-boundary concern with a measured verifier-input precondition. The normal separation works: environment/Dockerfile:9-15 installs only app packages and copies instructions/assets, task.toml:28 sets separate, and tests/Dockerfile:43-44 protects /tests. A fresh agent-image run found no /tests, /solution, RewardKit package, or rewardkit/claude/codex/playwright-mcp commands. Actual unchanged test.sh launched the ordinary-assets control at uid/gid 65534 with only DB_PATH, HOME, NODE_PATH, PATH and PORT; reads of criteria/scoring/root config/proc-1 environment/reward and write-open attempts to scorer/reward/CLI were denied, while SQLite insertion and HTTP serving succeeded. However task.toml:2 declares both /app and /assets as artifacts; test.sh:72-83 validates symlinks only under /app, then line 88 runs `chmod -R a+rX /assets`. When the verifier-input /assets is a symlink to /tests, that exact command traverses it, changing /tests from 0700 to 0755; the actual unprivileged submitted app then read /tests/scoring.toml, /tests/scored/functional/judge.toml and /tests/gates/render/judge.toml. Their observed hashes exactly matched frozen 95f70d6e..., 49c966b9..., and 4f4ac012... bytes. Source and image identity were independently verified in the fresh execution: all 15 /tests files matched before running; verifier image sha256:a6e377e2468671fe2b676f3d211ca5c0cfdc4b68a98cffd1349b332ed59c6251 and agent image sha256:ebdf6741fc24b580831365e3b3f1501571257715089d56f3213861da7ae23375 agree with the hash-verified raw artifact-binding record. The offending test.sh is byte-equal to the frozen template (bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa); this is not a task-specific divergence. Raw results: per-row-review/evidence/46/isolation-results.json SHA256 cc8892bd653a8a5039c526e063e8cef19efaa9d9eb34c6de55ee421d234eb194; driver SHA256 92253149cf6c2521559b70ec1a500226c666fb8da33c34283a0a5dc98a1311f4. Network was disabled; the local RewardKit transport stub exits 19, and the real harness retained zero reward. No real credential was supplied/read/output, no reward write succeeded, no configured grade or hosted exploit is claimed. Hosted/artifact-export replay of this root symlink remains unmeasured, so end-to-end reachability is explicitly unresolved rather than assumed.
counterexample: A malicious submission leaves an ordinary /app/server.js that probes private grading files, and arranges the exported artifact root /assets as a symlink to /tests. If artifact transfer preserves that symlink, the current verifier itself relaxes the rubric permissions before starting the app, allowing the app to tailor behavior to the exact criteria. The isolated test reproduces the exposure at verifier input but does not establish hosted transfer reachability or a resulting grade. integration.md:16-19 tells a conforming app to use ordinary files and constrains supported symlinks; the malicious case violates that convention, which is not an enforced /assets security boundary. The ordinary-files alternative was tested and could write SQLite/serve HTTP without acquiring private access; no isolation-caused failure of that control was observed.
suggested_fix: Escalate for a canonical harness/artifact-transfer fix that rejects symlinked artifact roots before any recursive permissions change (with an ordinary-files control), or provide measured evidence that the actual artifact exporter rejects/canonicalizes this exact root-symlink case; preserve the current task/template bytes until that policy change is authorized.
